summary: Request for written confirmation of data retention + deletion behavior (Hosted API) for security review
related_confluence_pages: Security & Compliance > Data Residency and Retention > Data Retention Controls (One-Pager)
Security & Compliance > Compliance Evidence > Customer Security Review Process (restricted)
description:
Customer (Northbridge) requested written confirmation of Redwood Inference data retention and deletion behavior for their vendor security review.

Request (from customer):
- Confirm whether prompts/outputs are stored and for how long.
- Confirm retention for application logs/telemetry and audit logs.
- Confirm whether Redwood can delete customer data on request and the expected timeline.
- Confirm any differences if they move from Hosted to Dedicated/Private.

Impact:
- Procurement/security review is blocked pending written statement.
- Customer wants a document suitable to attach to their questionnaire and internal approval ticket.

Notes:
- Support should not provide custom legal commitments. Route to GRC for approved language and/or security addendum references.

Internal references:
- Use enablement kit v2 retention one-pager as the primary customer-facing artifact.
- If customer requests SOC 2 report / evidence, follow the Customer Security Review Process SOP (restricted) and NDA requirements.

Customer point of contact:
- Security Analyst (name redacted in ticket)

Attachments:
- Customer questionnaire excerpt pasted in comments (see Comment 2).
comments: 2026-02-11 09:12 PT — Rachel Kim (Reporter): Customer asked for a written statement they can attach to their internal security review. They specifically want confirmation on: (1) whether prompts/completions are retained, (2) how long logs are retained, and (3) whether we can delete all data upon request. They also asked if Dedicated changes anything. Can GRC provide the approved language? Looping in Daniel Carter for evidence + wording pointers.

2026-02-11 09:20 PT — Rachel Kim: Questionnaire excerpt from customer:
"Does the vendor store customer-submitted data (including prompts, outputs, files) after request completion? If yes, what is the retention period? Can retention be configured? Describe deletion process and timelines."

2026-02-11 10:03 PT — Daniel Carter (Assignee): Acknowledged. We should respond with the approved customer-facing one-pager + clarify shared responsibility boundaries by deployment mode. I’ll draft a reply using the enablement kit language and route to Olga (GRC) for sign-off before we send anything that reads like a commitment.

2026-02-11 11:18 PT — Daniel Carter: Draft response (internal):
- Reference the customer-facing “Data Retention Controls” one-pager (v2) as the canonical statement.
- Explicitly note that retention can vary by data category (service logs vs audit logs vs customer content) and by deployment mode.
- Avoid ‘always/never’ language; keep it factual and tie to configuration where available.
- Offer to provide additional evidence (SOC 2, pen test summary) under NDA via the Security Review Process.

Requesting GRC approval before sending.
@Olga Petrov please review the below language (see next comment).

2026-02-11 11:19 PT — Daniel Carter: Proposed customer email language:

“Thanks for the questions — Redwood Inference provides documented retention and deletion behavior by data category and deployment mode.

For a written reference suitable for your security review, please see our ‘Data Retention Controls’ one‑pager (attached / link). It describes (a) retention defaults, (b) configurable retention where available, and (c) the process for deletion requests.

At a high level, retention behavior differs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and is subject to your configuration and contractual terms. If you share which deployment mode you’re evaluating (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), we can point you to the relevant sections.

If you need audit log retention details or compliance evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report), we can provide those under NDA via our security review process.”

(End draft)

2026-02-12 08:41 PT — Olga Petrov (GRC): Approved with one change: remove “subject to contractual terms” phrasing and replace with “as applicable to your agreement” to avoid sounding like we’re withholding info. Also add a line that deletion request timelines are communicated during the request intake and may vary based on data category and deployment mode. Do not provide a guaranteed timeline in writing unless Legal adds it to the security appendix.

2026-02-12 09:10 PT — Rachel Kim: Sent response to customer with the approved language + attached the ‘Data Retention Controls’ one‑pager. Also offered a follow-up call with Solutions Engineering if they want a deeper walkthrough of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private boundaries.

2026-02-12 09:12 PT — Rachel Kim: Link shared with customer (customer-facing): Confluence page “Data Retention Controls (One-Pager)” (latest). Internal note: ensure we’re sharing the external-safe PDF export from the enablement kit folder if they can’t access Confluence.

2026-02-13 14:26 PT — Rachel Kim: Customer follow-up: they asked whether Redwood can confirm ‘no training’ / ‘no model improvement’ using their prompts. I replied that this is covered in the Security FAQ v2 and offered to share the relevant excerpt; did not go beyond approved language. If they need formal language in the MSA/DPA, we will route to Legal.

2026-02-14 10:02 PT — Daniel Carter: Confirmed customer received the one-pager and accepted it for their questionnaire attachment. No additional evidence requested at this time. If they ask for SOC 2 report, route through the NDA workflow.
resolution: Provided customer with approved, customer-facing ‘Data Retention Controls’ one-pager (enablement kit v2) and an email response using GRC-approved language. Avoided custom commitments on deletion timelines; clarified that timelines are communicated during deletion request intake and may vary by data category and deployment mode. Ticket resolved after customer confirmed receipt and acceptance for their security review packet.
